title: Kenny Kersey's piano prank and the meat cleaver mix-up
summary: During the last night, pianist Kenny Kersey lifts the piano with his feet and Ben glares at Leeman, who later runs for the meat cleaver and is tackled by bandmates who think he is after Kersey.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: However, the story -- while we were on the stand in the last couple of sets, Kenny Kersey who, after a few beers or so, was more or less of a prankster, and the piano was going out of tune, and they didn't care, of course, because they were closing -- and he had long legs, and he had a way where he could lift the piano up with his legs and his feet, and let it down suddenly and make a thump.

Well, he did this a couple of times, and Ben Webster was busy playing and turned around and glared at me a couple of times, good friends as we were. He was just about to get pretty ornery, and Kenny did it a couple more times, so I screamed at Kenny and I said, "Don't do that, dammit, don't do that. I'm getting blamed for this" I was thinking, and

Kenny thought that was funny. So one or two more clumbs, and Ben looked at me. So when the set was over, I screamed at Kenny, and the guys in the band didn't quite know what was going on, but they knew that we were having an argument.

So when the set was over, we were done, the place was closing, and I had it all prearranged for myself to get a couple of those beautiful pots in to my bass drum case, and then I ran before it was too late -- I was gonna put them in my snare drum case -- I ran for the meat cleaver.

Well, I hope you find it as funny as I think is is, because it really was -- the band, Ben Webster, who was always known to be quite capable of throwing his weight around, and Eddie Barefield, especially, who has been in training for what, I don't know, for some 60 years, they grabbed me. Everybody was positively sure that I was after Kenny Kersey with a meat cleaver! Maybe the way I've told it doesn't strike you as being funny, but I had taken a lot of explaining so I could get that meat cleaver in the drum case!

I think you explained that beautifully, Cliff. That must have been quite some scene; I can just see all those dudes grabbing you, thinking, well, okay, here goes a piano player. That was quite funny -- and I'm glad you still have that meat cleaver.
